content: Deconditioning refers to the physiological changes that occur when an organism adapts to a less demanding environment or experiences a reduction in its normal physiological adaptations. Deconditioning can arise from various factors, including reduced physical activity, prolonged bed rest as prescribed in medical settings, immobilization due to orthopedic casting, paralysis, the natural aging process, and other similar conditions. In the field of aerospace medicine, deconditioning is of particular concern. It is studied extensively to identify, mitigate, and prevent the adverse physiological effects associated with the unique conditions of space flight. When deconditioning occurs as a result of reduced physical activity, it leads to a loss of muscle mass, which includes the atrophy of cardiac muscle.
